rationale:
Evidence: the iteration-1 race (60 trials, 0 finishes) gave oval progress 0.24, s-bend 0.14 and slalom 0.10. Max error was 0.064 to 0.067 m on the oval and slalom, above the 0.06 m limit. rms_error stayed at 0.025 to 0.029 m, so the robot tracks well on average and fails on peak excursions. Line losses were 1 to 2 per run, and steering_oscillation was 0.14 to 0.21.

Accepted from the round-1 critique: (a) the claim that spreading the outer sensors to x = 0.05 makes the outer pair engage earlier was wrong. Engagement distance is about |x| minus the footprint and tape half-widths, so the wider spread engages later. I drop the geometry change and return to the iteration-1 layout (x = -0.024 to 0.024, 0.012 m spacing, 0.016 m footprints, y = 0.05), which is the raced baseline. (b) kd 1.2 is not supported by the data: in iteration 1 kd moved from 0.3 to 0.8 and oscillation did not fall. I keep kd at 0.3 rather than raising it. (c) cutting kp to 3.0 reduces turn authority at the exact points where the robot leaves the tape, so I reject it.

Change: kp 6.0 to 7.0. This is the single change I pre-stated in iteration 1: if max_error stays above 0.06 m, raise kp by 1. Everything else (base_speed 1.4, ki 0.1, kd 0.3, geometry, last_direction) is held fixed, so the next race attributes any change in max_error, line losses and progress to kp alone. I keep base_speed at 1.4 because cutting it further would lower average speed toward the 1.5 m/s the finish needs.

Hypotheses: max_error falls below 0.06 m on the oval and slalom, line_loss_events fall to 1 or fewer per run, and progress rises above 0.25 on the oval. If steering_oscillation rises by more than 50 percent with kp 7, the next step is kd 0.1 to 0.2 on its own, not a higher kd. If line losses stay at 2 or more with max_error still high, the next test is line_loss 'search_right' alone. Slalom is the weakest track, so I judge the result on it as well.
